title: Telemetry Gatekeeper: Onboarding & QBR Integration Guide
author: Aisha Gupta
content:
SUMMARY

This guide defines the Telemetry Gatekeeper contract used during enterprise onboarding and quarterly business reviews (QBRs). It standardizes the telemetry, custom metrics, and validation checks we require before go-live and for QBR-ready reporting. The intent is to reduce onboarding time, prevent metric drift, and ensure customers and Customer Success (CS) teams have a shared, auditable signal set for availability, cost, latency, and quality.

SCOPE & AUDIENCE

- Scope: Redwood-hosted and Dedicated deployments where customers integrate service metrics or forward custom application signals. Covers metric schema, ingestion verification, dashboards, alert thresholds, and QBR-ready exports.
- Audience: Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Enterprise Dev/Ops teams, Observability Engineers, and Account Execs preparing QBRs.

WHY A TELEMETRY GATEKEEPER?

Onboarding often stalls on mismatched telemetry expectations. Telemetry Gatekeeper provides a small, enforceable contract so we can:

1. Validate that SLAs and SLOs are measurable from day one.
2. Ensure consistent cost attribution (per-route/per-model) for enterprise billing.
3. Enable objective QBR metrics with minimal custom instrumentation.

OWNERSHIP & CONTACTS

- Telemetry Gatekeeper owner: Customer Success (Aisha Gupta)
- Platform integration contact: Eng Platform (Marcus Patel)
- Observability SME: Eng SRE (Leah Browne)
- Customer success lead (customer-side): provided during kickoff

PREREQUISITES BEFORE ONBOARDING CHECKPOINT

1. Customer can forward metrics to one of the supported collectors: Prometheus remote_write, Datadog, or a secure S3/Parquet export for batch ingestion.
2. Customer has agreed on the telemetry retention window for plant/usage signals (default 90 days).
3. Access: Redwood CS/Platform has read-only access to the metrics workspace or a credentials-based ingest token.

TELEMETRY GATEKEEPER CONTRACT (REQUIRED SIGNALS)

Required signals are grouped by category. Each metric must include labels/tags: customer_id, deployment_type (hosted|dedicated|private), region, model_name, route. Timestamps in UTC.

1) Availability & Capacity
- redwood.request.count (counter): total requests, labeled by route, model_name
- redwood.request.errors (counter): error_count segmented by code, route
- redwood.instance.healthy (gauge): 0|1 per server/pool id (optional for private)

2) Latency & P95/P99
- redwood.request.latency_ms (histogram or summary): per route and model_name
- redwood.request.kvcache_hit_rate (gauge): percentage [0-1] per model variant

3) Cost & Usage Attribution
- redwood.tokens.generated (counter): per request, with token_count label
- redwood.embedding.units (counter): if embeddings used, with vector_dim label
- redwood.batch.size (histogram): batch sizes for throughput analysis

4) Quality Signals (optional, recommended for QBR)
- customer.eval.score (gauge): application-level quality metric, tied to a named prompt-set
- customer.prompt.latent_failures (counter): domain-specific failure modes to surface regressions

SAMPLE METRIC SCHEMA (Prometheus exposition)

# HELP redwood_request_latency_ms request latency in ms
# TYPE redwood_request_latency_ms histogram
redwood_request_latency_ms_bucket{le="100",route="/v1/generate",model_name="gpt-j-quant",customer_id="acme-corp"} 42
redwood_request_latency_ms_sum{route="/v1/generate",model_name="gpt-j-quant",customer_id="acme-corp"} 8243
redwood_request_latency_ms_count{route="/v1/generate",model_name="gpt-j-quant",customer_id="acme-corp"} 123

INGESTION & VALIDATION STEPS (ONBOARDING CHECKPOINTS)

We break validation into three automated checkpoints and one manual review:

1) Collector connectivity check (Day 0-1):
- Verify connectivity with remote_write / Datadog API / S3 ingest.
- Expected result: first metric appears within 15 minutes.
- Tooling: telemetry-checker-cli send-sample --endpoint <endpoint> --customer acme-corp

2) Label & Schema validation (Day 1):
- Automated script validates presence of required labels and types.
- Expected: 100% of incoming series have customer_id and route labels.

3) Baseline signal sanity (Day 1-3):
- Compare incoming metrics to expected ranges. Example: request.count > 10/day for active customers.
- Flag anomalies for manual triage.

4) Manual dashboard + SLO review (Day 3-7):
- CS and SRE review dashboards and sign-off on go/no-go.
- Sign-off template included in this doc.

AUTOMATED VALIDATION RULES (EXAMPLES)

- Missing required label: FAIL
- Requests reported but tokens.generated missing: WARNING
- P95 latency > 2000ms for 10%+ of routes: ALERT (triage)

SAMPLE VALIDATION COMMANDS

# Validate schema and labels (CLI)
telemetry-checker validate-schema --source prom --customer acme-corp --required-labels customer_id,route,model_name

# Run baseline sanity check
telemetry-checker baseline --customer acme-corp --window 24h --expected-min-requests 10

DASHBOARDS & QBR METRICS (RECOMMENDED PANELS)

Minimum QBR-ready dashboards:
- Traffic & Errors: total requests, 7d trend, errors by code and route
- Latency Slices: P50/P95/P99 by model and route, broken down by region
- Cost Attribution: tokens.generated and embeddings.units per route and model, month-to-date
- Quality Signals: customer.eval.score trend and regressions by prompt-set
- Capacity & Autoscaling: instance utilization, queue lengths, batch sizes

SAMPLE PROMETHEUS QUERIES

- Total requests (7d): sum(increase(redwood_request_count[7d])) by (route)
- P95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model_name))
- Token rate: sum(rate(redwood_tokens_generated[1m])) by (route, customer_id)

QBR SLIDE TEMPLATE (METRICS WE PULL)

1. Executive summary (uptime %, cost delta month-over-month, key wins)
2. Availability & Latency trends (P95, P99)
3. Cost per 1k tokens and cost drivers by route/model
4. Quality snapshot (customer.eval.score and top 3 prompt regressions)
5. Action items and runbook changes for next quarter

ALERTING & ESCALATION (TELEMETRY DISCREPANCIES)

Default thresholds (suggested; tune per-customer):
- Availability: redwood.request.errors / redwood.request.count > 0.02 for 5m -> P1 on-call
- Latency: P95 > 2s for 10% routes in 10m -> P1 on-call
- Token anomaly: token rate increase > 3x baseline in 15m without corresponding traffic -> P0 security/cost

Escalation steps:
1) Automated ticket created in Zendesk with metric snapshot and link to dashboard.
2) CS owns initial customer communication within 30 minutes.
3) If P1/P0, page SRE and Solutions Eng. Use dedicated escalation channel: #escalations-enterprise-telemetry.

HANDOFF CHECKLIST (GO-LIVE)

- [ ] Collector confirmed and sample data present
- [ ] Schema validation passed (labels/types)
- [ ] Dashboards created and shared with customer
- [ ] Alerts configured and SLOs mapped to on-call responders
- [ ] Cost attribution verified for top 5 routes
- [ ] CS sign-off documented

EXAMPLE CS SIGN-OFF NOTE

We, the undersigned, confirm that the Telemetry Gatekeeper contract is satisfied for customer ACME CORP. Dashboards: <link>. Alerts: <link>. Signed: Customer Success Owner (Aisha Gupta) & Customer Eng Lead (name). Date: YYYY-MM-DD.

DISCREPANCY TRIAGE RUNBOOK (WHEN METRICS LOOK OFF)

1) Confirm ingestion endpoint and timestamps (time skew issues are common).
2) Check labels: if missing customer_id, try re-ingest with relabeled source or apply relabeling rule in Prometheus remote_write.
3) If tokens.generated is zero but request.count > 0: check model routing and inference runtime for missing instrumentation (file a runtime bug).
4) For noisy spikes, compute request/token delta: spike in tokens without requests implies billing/abuse — escalate to security.

REPORTING & QBR PREPARATION (CS OPERATIONS)

- Weekly telemetry snapshot emailed to AE and customer 2 weeks before QBR.
- Pull standard artifacts 3 days before QBR: traffic CSV, cost CSV, quality eval exports (JSON), dashboard PDFs.
- Responsibility matrix: CS prepares executive summary; Solutions Eng prepares technical root cause slides; SRE validates production signals.

TEMPLATED ARTIFACTS (copy for CS)

1) Telemetry validation sign-off (Google Doc link template)
2) Dashboard export checklist (CSV of queries)
3) QBR metrics export script (CLI example):

# Export tokens per route last 30 days
telemetry-export --query "sum(increase(redwood_tokens_generated[30d])) by (route, model_name)" --format csv --customer acme-corp --out tokens_30d.csv

SECURITY & DATA SENSITIVITY NOTES

- Do not forward PII. All metrics must be anonymized; free-text prompt fields must be redacted.
- For private deployments, prefer VPC-native collectors and role-limited service principals.

TIMELINE RECOMMENDATION

- Day 0: Kickoff and collector access established
- Day 1-3: Connectivity + schema validation
- Day 3-7: Dashboard build and CS/SRE sign-off
- Week 2: Go-live and 7-day monitoring window

APPENDIX: COMMON TROUBLESHOOTING SNIPPETS

1) Prometheus relabel example to add customer_id:

- job_name: redwood_remote_write
  static_configs:
  - targets: ['collector.example.com:9091']
  relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__address__]
    target_label: customer_id
    replacement: acme-corp

2) Datadog forwarding note: ensure "host" tag is stable and not ephemeral. Use container_id label instead for grouping.

FEEDBACK & ITERATION

This guide is versioned by Customer Success. Send feedback or improvement requests to the Telemetry Gatekeeper owner or open a PR in the onboarding playbook repo.
